 Free agency is well underway in Major League Baseball, with the Boston Red Sox making one of the biggest early splashes by landing Jake Bowers on a 4-year deal.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement More decisions are to come before the expected lockout at the beginning of December, with the latest being a former Red Sox starter deciding to join an American League contender in the Chicago White Sox.
 According to the latest report from Robert Murray, right-hander Dustin May has signed a 3-year deal worth more than $ 50 million.
 "BREAKING: Free-agent pitcher Dustin May and the Chicago White Sox are in agreement on a three-year contract worth just north of $50 million, according to sources familiar with the deal," Murray reported .
 May, 29 years old, has above-average stuff. He can throw it with the best of them in terms of pure stuff, but his base numbers haven't exactly been the best throughout his career.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Red Sox found that out during the 2025 campaign when he posted a 5.40 ERA and walked 13 in 28.1 innings. However, there's been hope throughout his career that he can put everything together and be the dominant arm that people expect.
 He has an elite fastball and above-average extension, but hasn't been able to put away hitters at the level we'd all expect. In 2026, he had a 49th-percentile chase % and a 32nd-percentile whiff %.
 The White Sox, who were one of the better teams in Major League Baseball last season, which came as a surprise to many, are looking to improve on both sides of the baseball this winter.
 May doesn't guarantee anything, but Chicago looks like a legitimate team that can threaten teams like the Red Sox heading into 2027 and beyond.
